1311.quote_or_event: “The One God is our father; we are the children of the One God. You are our Guru.”
1311.explanation: Guru Arjan teaches that God belongs equally to all people, who are all His children.
1311.tie_back: The Kural's wife will not come near a chest she says all women gaze on as common property; Gurbani, by contrast, rejoices that the Lord is shared by all, with no room for jealousy.
1311.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 611, Raag Sorath, Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1311._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best, by contrast: the Kural's playful jealousy over a love shared by many has no Sikh parallel; Gurbani celebrates the Lord belonging to all.

1312.quote_or_event: “Good omens and bad omens affect those who do not keep the Lord in the mind.”
1312.explanation: Guru Arjan teaches that one who remembers God is not ruled by signs and omens.
1312.tie_back: The Kural's husband sneezes to force his sulking wife to speak the customary blessing; Gurbani sets aside such customs around signs, saying they bind only those who forget God.
1312.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 401, Raag Aasaa, Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1312._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: relevant to the sneeze custom the Kural relies on, but the Kural's scene is playful, not about superstition, and Sikhism rejects such omens.

1313.quote_or_event: “O soul-bride, without your Husband Lord, what good are your decorations?”
1313.explanation: Guru Nanak teaches that the soul's adornments mean nothing unless they are for the Beloved.
1313.tie_back: The Kural's wife accuses her husband of wearing a garland to show some other woman; Gurbani also asks whom one's adornment is for, saying only the Beloved gives it meaning.
1313.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 18, Siree Raag, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1313._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: both turn on who an adornment is meant for, but the Kural's jealousy theme is absent. This is spiritual love for God, not romantic love.

1314.quote_or_event: “You are the Primal Being, the Most Wonderful Creator. There is no other as Great as You.”
1314.explanation: Guru Ram Das declares that God has no equal and cannot be compared with anyone.
1314.tie_back: The Kural's wife bristles at 'more than anyone', as if her husband were ranking her against others; Gurbani's praise of the Beloved avoids ranking because no one can stand beside Him.
1314.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 11, So Purakh (Raag Aasaa), Guru Ram Das (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1314._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: both concern comparison with others in love, but Gurbani affirms God is beyond comparison rather than taking offence at it.

1315.quote_or_event: “This human body has been given to you. This is your chance to meet the Lord of the Universe.”
1315.explanation: Guru Arjan teaches that this present human life is the precious opportunity for union with God.
1315.tie_back: The Kural's husband promises they will not part in this birth and his wife weeps at the limit; Gurbani also treats this present life as the decisive time for union.
1315.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 12, Raag Aasaa, Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1315._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: both assume rebirth and stress this present life, but the Kural is about a misread promise, while Gurbani urges spiritual effort now.

1316.quote_or_event: “Chanting it, I live; forgetting it, I die.”
1316.explanation: Guru Nanak says remembering the Name is life and forgetting it is death.
1316.tie_back: The Kural's wife hears 'I thought of you' and asks, 'So you had forgotten me?'; Gurbani makes the same link between remembrance and forgetting central to love for God.
1316.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 9, So Dar (Raag Aasaa), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1316._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; reasonable: both turn on remembering versus forgetting the beloved; in Gurbani it is naam simran, not a lovers' quibble. This is spiritual love for God, not romantic love.

1317.quote_or_event: “Only idiots and fools worry about these omens and days.”
1317.explanation: Guru Amar Das dismisses worry over omens and auspicious days as foolishness.
1317.tie_back: The Kural's wife reads a sneeze as a sign that another woman is thinking of her husband; Gurbani rejects reading meaning into such signs.
1317.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 843, Raag Bilaaval (Vaar Sat), Guru Amar Das (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1317._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: directly relevant to the sneezing belief behind the couplet, but the Kural uses it for humour, not as teaching.

1318.quote_or_event: “Even without our speaking, He knows everything.”
1318.explanation: Guru Nanak says the Lord knows our inner state without our telling Him.
1318.tie_back: The Kural's wife accuses her husband of hiding who is thinking of him; Gurbani reminds that nothing can be hidden from the One who knows every heart.
1318.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 661, Raag Dhanaasree, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1318._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: shares the theme of hidden thoughts, but the Kural's suspicion is playful and human, while Gurbani speaks of God's knowledge.

1319.quote_or_event: “O Nanak, the Husband Lord enjoys His bride when she is pleasing to His Mind.”
1319.explanation: Guru Nanak teaches that union comes to the soul-bride who pleases the Lord, not to one who frets about others.
1319.tie_back: The Kural's wife grows angry that her husband must soothe other women the same way; Gurbani turns the bride's attention from rivals to being pleasing herself.
1319.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 243, Raag Gauree, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1319._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: both concern a bride's relation to a beloved shared by others, but Gurbani has no jealousy and the love is spiritual. This is spiritual love for God, not romantic love.

1320.quote_or_event: “Wherever I look, I see only You. The True Guru has inspired me to see You.”
1320.explanation: Guru Nanak describes a gaze so filled with the Beloved that he sees Him everywhere.
1320.tie_back: The Kural's wife asks whom her husband is thinking of as he gazes; in Gurbani the devotee's gaze holds only the Beloved, the very single-mindedness she wants.
1320.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 55, Siree Raag, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1320._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: both centre on whom one's gaze holds, but the Kural's humour of suspicion has no Sikh counterpart. This is spiritual love for God, not romantic love.
